items.title: The Hamilton-Jacobi equation of a declared potential presentation: the class of action-dimension functions $S$ with $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ in one momentum chart
items.physical_scope: The Hamilton-Jacobi equation of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch, read in one of the presentation's momentum charts: the class of $C^3$ functions $S$ of the chart variables $(t,q,\alpha)$ that satisfy $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ for the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of that chart, together with the action dimension of $S$ and the dependence of the equation on the declared chart, inverse Legendre branch and potential representative. The item defines a function class relative to that datum; it asserts no existence of solutions, no equation of motion for the model, no completeness of any flow and no measured value.

items.title: A complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation: nondegenerate mixed derivative, momentum map and Jacobi constants
items.physical_scope: The complete-integral datum of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: a $C^3$ solution $S$ of the presentation's Hamilton-Jacobi equation in a fixed momentum chart whose mixed derivative $S_{q\alpha}$ is invertible at the base point, together with its momentum map $p=S_q$ and its Jacobi constants $\beta=S_\alpha$, their dimensions and their reading as a family of model data labelled by the parameters $\alpha$. The item defines the datum only; the constancy of the Jacobi constants along the characteristic motions, the local solvability of the constants equation and the canonicity of $(\beta,\alpha)$ are theorems of this page, not part of the definition, and no existence or measured value is asserted.

items.title: Completely integrable data of a declared presentation: $n$ smooth phase functions with $F_1=H$, pairwise in involution and independent on the regular locus
items.physical_scope: Complete integrability of the Hamiltonian system of a declared hyperregular potential presentation: a datum of $n$ phase functions on an open phase domain of dimension $2n$, with first entry the branch Hamiltonian, pairwise in involution, independent on an open dense regular locus, and the attached integral map, regular values and regular fibres; the datum is a completely integrable Hamiltonian system for the presentation's two-form in the root-library sense. The item defines the datum class; it asserts no model of the force branch is completely integrable, no fibre structure, no action-angle coordinates and no measured value.

items.title: A complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation produces the model's motions, its Jacobi constants and local canonical $(\beta,\alpha)$ labels
items.physical_scope: The characteristics theorem of the Hamilton-Jacobi method for a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: from a complete integral of the presentation's Hamilton-Jacobi equation in a fixed momentum chart, the characteristic curves of the equation solve the chart's Hamilton equations; on the potential branch they are motions of the model; the derivatives of the complete integral in the parameters are constant along them; a local converse solves the constants equation for the configuration; and the Jacobi data are local canonical coordinates of the presentation's two-form. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it is local in the time, configuration and parameter variables, assumes the nondegeneracy of the mixed derivative at the base point only, and asserts no global solution, no completeness and no empirical content.

items.title: Compact connected regular fibres of a completely integrable datum of the presentation are Lagrangian tori with a full period lattice
items.physical_scope: The fibre structure of a completely integrable datum of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: a compact connected regular common fibre of the integral map is an embedded Lagrangian submanifold generically spanned by the datum's Hamiltonian fields, carries the commuting-field local action of the cited mathematics as a transitive complete action with a full stabilizer lattice, and is diffeomorphic to a torus. The conclusion is conditional on the datum's smoothness, involution, independence on the regular locus, the compactness, connectedness and regularity of the fibre, and on the Axiom of Countable Choice through the cited lattice lemma; it asserts no global fibration, no action-angle coordinates, no completeness of flows off the compact fibre and no empirical content.

items.title: Action-angle coordinates of a completely integrable presentation: period-one angles, action coordinates, $H=h(I)$ and linear motion on the tori
items.physical_scope: Action-angle coordinates for a completely integrable datum of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: near a compact connected regular fibre and over a ball of regular values on which the integral map is a proper submersion with connected fibres, there are period-one angle and action coordinates of the presentation's two-form with $\omega=\sum_i d\theta_i\wedge dI_i$; fibrewise-constant functions, in particular the datum and the branch Hamiltonian, depend on the actions alone; and the model's motions become the constant-action, linear-angle flows. The conclusion is conditional on the Axiom of Countable Choice, on the complete integrability of the datum and on all the fibre hypotheses; it is local over the ball of regular values, asserts no global coordinates on the phase domain, and carries no empirical content. The identification of the coordinates with classical period integrals is a normalization convention, not part of the theorem.

items.title: Adiabatic invariance of the action of a slowly varying one-frequency model: an order-$\varepsilon$ drift bound on the $O(1/\varepsilon)$ time scale
items.physical_scope: Adiabatic invariance of the action coordinate of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch when the model carries a slow real parameter: if in a period-one action-angle chart the branch Hamiltonian is $h(I,s)+\varepsilon k(I,\theta,s)$ with nonvanishing frequency $|\partial_Ih|\ge\omega_0$ and the parameter runs as $s(t)=s_0+\varepsilon t$, then along every model solution that stays in the compact chart region the action changes by at most the displayed order-$\varepsilon$ bound on $0\le t\le A/\varepsilon$. The statement is conditional on the existence of the uniform parameter-dependent action-angle chart, on the frequency bound and on the trapping of the solution; it asserts no exact invariance, no statement across a separatrix or a chart boundary, and no empirical content.

items.title: Scope of the Hamilton-Jacobi and integrability statements: locality, the fibre hypotheses, global obstructions and the frequency conventions
items.physical_scope: The recorded scope of the Hamilton-Jacobi and integrability items of this page: the local character of the Hamilton-Jacobi construction and of its no-caustic hypothesis; the separate requirements of involution and independence in complete integrability; the compactness, connectedness, regularity and proper-submersion hypotheses of the torus and action-angle conclusions together with their Countable-Choice assumption; the published monodromy obstruction to global action-angle coordinates; and the period-one versus radian frequency convention. The remark asserts no new mathematical claim and no empirical content; it is a scope record for the conditional deductions of this page.

items.title: The harmonic model worked through: an explicit complete integral, its characteristic motion, and the action-angle chart with $I=\oint p\,dx$ and period-one frequency $1/T$
items.physical_scope: A worked instance of the Hamilton-Jacobi and action-angle items inside the declared harmonic model of the framework's force branch: for one label of mass $m>0$ and spring constant $k>0$, the explicit family $S$ is a complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation wherever $\sin(\omega t)\neq0$; its characteristic curves are the harmonic motions with $\beta=S_\alpha$ constant; and the explicit chart $(\theta,I)$ is canonical with $H=I/T$, $\dot I=0$, $\dot\theta=1/T$ and $I=\oint p\,dx$, in the period-one convention, with the radian rescaling recovering the sources' chart. The example asserts no measured value, no claim that a real oscillator realizes the model, and no global extension of $S$ across the conjugate times $\omega t\in\pi\mathbb Z$.

items.title: The gravitational two-body model on an elliptic orbit: two simple turning points of the effective potential and $J_{\mathrm a}'(E)=T/(2\pi)=\sqrt{\mu/\kappa}\,a^{3/2}$
items.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the orbit suppliers, A worked instance inside the two-label gravitational model of the framework's force branch: for an elliptic relative orbit ($j=Je_3$, $J>0$, $E<0$, eccentricity $0\le e<1$), the Kepler effective potential has exactly two simple turning points on the energy window between its minimum and $0$; the one-dimensional action variable of the radial problem is $C^1$ there with derivative $T/(2\pi)$; and the radial quadrature is the orbital period, so $J_{\mathrm a}'(E)=T/(2\pi)=\sqrt{\mu/\kappa}\,a^{3/2}$ with $T^2=4\pi^2\mu a^3/\kappa$. The example uses only the model's declared couplings $\kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1^{g}m_2^{g}$ and masses; no measured value of $G_{\mathrm N}$ and no empirical premise is used, and no real orbit is claimed to obey the model.

items.title: The zero-energy level of the harmonic model: a compact connected common level set of a completely integrable datum that is a point, not a torus
items.physical_scope: A counterexample inside the declared harmonic model of the framework's force branch: the one-label harmonic datum $(H)$ on the whole Cartesian phase plane is a completely integrable datum, and its zero common level set is compact, connected and nonempty but consists of the single rest point, so it is not diffeomorphic to a torus; equivalently, the level is a critical level at which the regular-fibre hypotheses of the torus theorem fail. The item asserts no measured value and no claim about any apparatus; it shows that regularity cannot be dropped from the hypotheses.

items.title: A free label: a nonempty regular common level set of a completely integrable datum that is noncompact and has no period lattice
items.physical_scope: A counterexample inside the zero-force potential presentation of the framework's force branch: the one-label free datum $(H)$ with $H=|p|^2/(2m)$ on the Cartesian phase domain is a completely integrable datum, and its positive-energy common level set is a nonempty regular level set that is unbounded, hence noncompact, and on which the Hamiltonian flow is free with trivial stabilizer, so no nonzero period and no full period lattice exist. The item asserts no measured value and no claim about any apparatus; it shows that compactness cannot be dropped from the torus and period-lattice conclusions.

items.title: The conjugate time of the harmonic model: the complete integral's mixed derivative is unbounded and the characteristic family refocuses at $\omega t\in\pi\mathbb Z$
items.physical_scope: A worked warning inside the declared harmonic model of the framework's force branch: the explicit complete integral of the oscillator's Hamilton-Jacobi equation is defined only on the time strips between the conjugate times $\omega t\in\pi\mathbb Z$; its mixed derivative $S_{x\alpha}=-m\omega\csc(\omega t)$ is unbounded as those times are approached; and the characteristic family through a fixed event refocuses there (all members with the same initial position pass through the same point a half-period later), so the map from the family's label to the position degenerates. The example asserts no measured value and no claim about any apparatus; it exhibits why the Hamilton-Jacobi statements of this page are local in time and carry no claim across a caustic.
